I would imagine that it was really necessary to reinforce or replace the forces of the Ministry of Interior in the area, which was a normal thing to do. So there is a direct link between the situation and this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And if I were to ask you the same question that I asked you earlier about the connection between this document and the operational control of the minister, would you give me the same response?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, I would, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P471.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn briefly back to your amended expert report, Mr. Bezruchenko, because I believe there is one passage that I neglected to review with you. If you could turn, please, to page 114. Actually, no, I believe I have -- I have gone over this with you. I will not go over it again. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to turn to a slightly different topic. If you could turn to what is tab 10 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is -- would be 65 ter 367.4. It is not specifically referred to in Mr. Bezruchenko's report, but because of the obvious relevance I would like to discuss this document with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a document from the office of the president of the Republic of Macedonia issued on the 28th of February, 2001. And you will see on the last page it is signed by the then president Boris Trajkovski. This date, 28 February 2001, why was that a significant date in Macedonia that year?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Well, I would say that, generally speaking, the month of February was a difficult period in 2001. In fact several days earlier, if I recall correctly, on or about 22nd of February, President Kostunica and the then president of Macedonia Trajkovski, endorsed an agreement about border delineation between Macedonia and Republic of Yugoslavia. In February, in fact early February, the military activities at the border also stepped up. There was some clashes between the security forces and the NLA. So analysing this document in the context of this developments I can say that this document in fact represents decision by the president of the country, as the supreme commander to reinforce the border and to deploy certain army units in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's talk about this a bit more slowly. The document reads: "Based on the annual plan of operations and training manual for 2001 and in order to conduct drills for the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia under winter conditions, the president orders, one, the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia should prepare and conduct training under winter conditions with a part of the commands and units according to the following." And then there are several army units that are listed below that. Point 3 says: "The exercise activities should be conducted in the direction Skopje (the army barracks) at Ilinden, Brodec, Ramno and then up to Kodra Fura." Can you explain to the Judges in general terms where Kodra Fura is?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Kodra Fura is the location north of Skopje right on the border with Kosovo and the name Kodra Fura is normally used in various documents of Macedonian government as the location indicating the border watch tower located in the area and manned by the border brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, if you take a look at paragraph 5 it says: "In case of attack upon the commands, units, positions and watch towers to act according to the Book of Rules for combat use. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you review this document given your expertise, how did you interpret this document, Mr. Bezruchenko? What was being ordered here?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: The document speaks about the exercise, winter training, but there are certain points about this document which should be explained in more detail. First of all, the exercises are supposed to take place in the area of Kodra Fura. It is not a coincidence this that specific area was selected for the exercise. As I mentioned before, clashes took place in the area and there were casualties inflicted on the Macedonian security forces. It is normal in any army in fact, to deploy forces in an area which is being threatened under cover of exercise, training activities, whereas the real purpose would be to deploy the forces, to develop the units, to familiarise with the terrain, to make the reconnaissance of the area. This would be my assessment of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So in your assessment, the instructions given in this document actually refer to the activities of the NLA close to the border. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I would imagine that this was the main reason for this document. And I would also like to specifically comment on point 5. "In case of attack upon the commands, units, positions, and watch towers to act according to the book of rules for combat use," which means that essentially the unit commanders were given rights to start combat actions, meaning to open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, why is it significant, if it is, that the president signed this order?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: The president was exercising his powers vested in the constitution as the commander in chief of the Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be Exhibit P472.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, could you please turn to what is tab 11 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 367.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document, Mr. Bezruchenko, is dated the 5th of March, 2001. It says military secret, state secret at the top. It is entitled use of the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, decision to be submitted. Signed by the president, Boris Trajkovski. And paragraph 1 of this decision says: "To give an appropriate response with all available information -- with all available formation armaments to the armed attacks and provocations by the diversion-terrorist groups upon the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." And then in paragraph 2 it says: "That the chief of the General Staff of the army ... Should regulate with his command the use of forces." Mr. Bezruchenko, why was this a significant document for you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This is a significant document because this is direct order by the president to the army as it is termed to respond with all available formation armaments to the armed attacks and provocations. Basically, it means that there were armed attacks and provocations on the part of the NLA against the army of the Republic of Macedonia. That is, the fighting was going on. Secondly, the units of the army were given the right to respond with all available formation armament. Formation armament in this sense would mean all the weapons the unit would have, according to the table of organisation and equipment of this specific unit. Which would also include perhaps if such units were deployed and I believe they were deployed, the artillery and mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be Exhibit P473.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't mean to be pedantic and overly technical, would it assist the Trial Chamber as I'm discussing these documents with Mr. Bezruchenko to also describe where -- which footnote in Mr. Bezruchenko's report the document is referred to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would, and I'm sure it would assist other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. The last document, Your Honour, that was admitted is referred to at paragraphs -- excuse me, footnotes 330 and 476 of the amended expert report and at footnote 12 of the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you turn to what is tab 12, please, of your binder, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this is 65 ter number 367.6.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is another decision signed by the president, Boris Trajkovski it is also dated the 5th of March, 2001. It is entitled, Raising the combat readiness of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, Decision to be submitted. And paragraph 1 of the decision says: "To carry out additional mobilisation of the 1st and 4th Guard Battalion, Guard Brigade. The mobilisation to be carried out immediately. The mobilised units are to be engaged to strengthen the system for security of the state border upon the decision of the commander of the 1st Guard Brigade." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraphs 2 tell us: "To engage the artillery battalion of the 1st Infantry Brigade, to strengthen the system of the state border." And then paragraph 3 says: "The entire peacetime composition of commands and units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to be put into a full combat readiness and their engagement to be carried out according to the development of the situation and upon the decision of the chief of General Staff." And before I ask you a question about this I should explain that this document is referred to in footnotes 330, 344, 412, 466, 475 of the amended expert report and also at footnote 11 in part 5 the chronology. Mr. Bezruchenko, why was this document significant for you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I believe this is a significant document because of a number of reasons. First of all, this is significant because it authorises the full combat readiness of the army, which presents an extraordinary development which takes place only in a situation of a pronounced threat against security of a country or any other major extraordinary situation. It is also important because it apparently indicates that the system of the security of the border was not strong enough and required additional mobilisation. It also indicates that the 1st Guard Brigade as printed, was not fully mobilised and additional mobilisation was required, again for the purposes of strengthening the border. It is apparent that the forces which were deployed in the area were apparently not sufficient to ensure this task. The document also speaks about the artillery battalion of this brigade to be deployed, which means that apparently the intensity of armed clashes or fighting reached such a level that required artillery to be deployed and used against the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be Exhibit P474.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, will you turn, please, to what is tab 13 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Exhibit 1D00-079. And this document is referred to in footnotes 330, 345, 477 of the amended expert report, and footnote 27 of the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this document is dated the 19th of March, 2001, signed by the president of the republic, Boris Trajkovski. And it is titled use of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to carry out an operation. Marked urgent, and it then says, decision: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia with all available units and means to carry out an operation to destroy the terrorists in the area of Tetovo." "The preparation of the units should start immediately, and the operation to be carried out at the latest by 20 March 2001." Why was this document significant for you, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This document has to be analysed in the context of the military developments or military situation in Macedonia at that time. As I mentioned previously, on 14th March, or on about 14th March, 2001, the NLA opened a front above Tetovo. This document, in fact, represents an order by the president of the country to carry out an operation in the area of Tetovo. Two things need to be explained in this sense. First of all, the document speaks of operation. Normally, according to classical military doctrine an operation is an action which is a level above an ordinary battle and will require involvement of units of a brigade size, or a regiment size, which means that certain significant forces had to be committed to carry out this operation. Second point which is also obvious from this document to me, is that the situation in the area of Tetovo was indeed pressing and urgent as the deadline to carry this operation out was the 20th of March. That is, the operation was supposed to be completed on the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise, it has already been received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can turn to what is tab 14 in your binder, please, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 367.12.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is another decision issued by the president of Macedonia at that time, Boris Trajkovski. It is dated the 20th of March, 2001. It's titled addendum to the decision DT number 07-15 of 19 March 2001, for the use of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to carry out an operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before I go any further, Your Honours, this document is referred to at footnotes 330 and 478 in Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report and footnote 31 of the chronology section, which is part 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this decision says in the middle of the first -- the top paragraph, above -- below the word urgent. It says: "In conformity with the newly established situation and need for additional reconnaissance and strengthening of the forces to break up and destroy the terrorists as soon as possible, I hereby bring the following decision." And paragraph 1 of the decision says: "The operation to break up and destroy the terrorists in the region of Tetovo to continue until final execution and establishing control over the territory." What did you take from this document, Mr. Bezruchenko, that was significant?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I believe this document is significant because a number of reasons. First of all, the document speaks about newly established situation which means that between the date the previous order had been issued and 20th of March, some radical changes in the situation occurred. Apparently, this situation did not really show any signs of improvement in the area of Tetovo, because in point 1 of this decision the president said that operation is to be continued until final execution, which means that the order which was previous -- which was issued only a day before was not carried out. And, again, this document speaks of control over the territory, which to me would serve as an indication that NLA was controlled at least some territory in this area, in the area of Tetovo, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, Mr. Bezruchenko, you said that this document indicates that the order which was issued only a day before was not carried out. Are you suggesting that the order issued by the president a day earlier was ignored?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: No, I'm not suggesting that. I'm just suggesting that perhaps due to the developments on the ground, the reality of the military situation, the forces, the security forces which were deployed in the area simply were not sufficient to carry out this operation and accomplish this mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be Exhibit P475.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 15 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Exhibit number 1D0080. And this document is referred to in footnotes 330, 346 and 479 of the amended expert report, and footnote 41 of the chronology chapter; it's part 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this document is another decision issued by the president Boris Trajkovski. He issued it on the 28th of March, 2001. It is entitled use of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to carry out an operation, decision to be submitted. And again in the first paragraph below the word urgent there is a reference to: "In conformity with the newly established situation and the need to break up and destroy the terrorists as soon as possible." Then there's the decision. And part 1 of the decision says this: "With all available units and means, the army of the Republic of Macedonia to carry out an operation to destroy the terrorists in the area of Kumanovo, the village Sopot, Kucingdelski and Zeden. And then it says: "The preparation of the units should start immediately and execution of the operation should start on the 28th of March, 2001." What significance, if any, did you find in this document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I believe this document is significant because, actually, it emphasises that the NLA was not really defeated in the previous operations by the security forces; but, on the contrary, the NLA gradually was spreading its territorial control to other areas of Macedonia. This document speaks about the Kumanovo and village of Sopot which is in the area of Kumanovo, which is quite a distance away from where the first front was opened which is Tetovo. This document also mentions Zeden which is a hill or, rather a ridge, mountain ridge, west of Skopje. My interpretation of this document is that NLA was apparently becoming active in this area -- in these areas as of the date of this document. I probably also can infer from this document that the situation was indeed pretty urgent as document speaks about an operation which is supposed to begin on the very day that the document was issued. That is, 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender -- excuse me, I made the same mistake. This document is already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, please, to what is tab 16 in your binder, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 367.23. It is referred to in footnotes 330, 347, 480 of the amended expert report, and footnote 57 of the chronology section.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this document, again, signed by the president Boris Trajkovski, dated now the 3rd of May, 2001. The use of the army of the Republic of Macedonia to carry out an operation. We see that this is urgent, same language about in conformity with the newly established situation. Then we see paragraph 1 of the decision says this: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia, in cooperation with the forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, to carry out an operation to destroy the terrorist forces in the wider region of the villages Vaksince and Slupcane, and in the other areas within the zones of responsibility where diversion terrorist groups appear." What, if anything, did you find significant in this decision, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, this is tab 17, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, this is tab 16.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated the 3rd of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Right, okay. The significance of this document is again based on the new locations which are mentioned in connection with the combat activities and these locations are villages of Vaksince and Slupcane, which are somewhat to the south of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is ERN N006-3997.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Sorry, not Tetovo. Kumanovo. This is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I still want to show this witness this map. It was admitted a short time ago, but I apologise, I did not write down the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 467 may be what you need, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's exactly what I need. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you need to put on your glasses, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I have a bit of a problem with my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do not be shy. Can you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would a hard copy assist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly would, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I can give the witness my own. I'm grateful, Your Honour, as I'm sure the witness is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village of Vaksince is actually to the north of Kumanovo and close to the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I assume that the village of Slupcane is in more or less the same area which would indicate to me that the area which was affected by fighting and military activities was gradually spreading around Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Going back to the document in paragraph 1, this document also -- mentioned the army of the Republic of Macedonia in coordination with the forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. What significance, if any, do you take from that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Well, these points would mean to me that the forces of the army alone would not be sufficient to carry out this kind of operation and would require the involvement of the forces under control of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe it is 1D50, Exhibit 1D50 already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is Exhibit 1D00-058. It is referred to in Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report at footnotes 330, 348, 481, and at footnote 92 of part 5, the chronology section.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is another document, another decision issued by the president of Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. This decision was issued on the 4th of June, 2001. Paragraph 1 of the decision says this: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia and the units of the ministry of internal affairs to prepare and carry out an attack operation in the wider region of Skopska Crna Gora, village Vujance, village Slupcane, village Opae, village Nikustak, village Matejce and village Strima, in order to surround, block, break up, and destroy the forces of diversion and terrorist groups with a simultaneous attack from several directions and a vertical manoeuvre, as well as to create continues for cleaning the terrain and to finally establish full control over the mentioned territory and the functioning of the local authorities." First of all, in general, what significance, if any, do you draw from this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: In general, the significance of the document would be as follows. The document clearly speaks about a serious military operation in the area of Skopska Crna Gora, and Skopska Crna Gora in fact a massive mountain area right above the capital of Skopje, north of Skopje. Which would mean to me that the fighting was gradually spreading from the area of Kumanovo towards Skopska Crna Gora, and probably further down south. The document speaks also about the missions that the Armed Forces are supposed to undertake and these are to surround, block, break up, and destroy the forces of the diversion and terrorist groups which means that the army was given a decisive task to put an end to the forces of the adversary, that is the NLA. An important point that I would also infer from this document is that deputy chief of General Staff of the army, Lieutenant-Colonel General Pande Petrovski, as well as the commander of the 1st Army Corps Major-General Georgi Karakutovski were apparently made personally responsible for this operation. I would also infer from this document that because of the seriousness of the situation, the responsibility was squarely placed on General Petrovski and General Karakutovski. Another point that I would like to infer from this document is that, apparently, this operation was supposed to involve the combat helicopters as it speaks about vertical manoeuvre and probably an airborne force was supposed to get involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you turn now to what is tab 18 in your binder, please, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is 65 ter 367.37. And this document is not specifically cited to in Mr. Bezruchenko's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is another document signed by the president, Boris Trajkovski, dated the 7th of June 2001. It is entitled mobilisation of a part of the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. And it says: "Orders." And in the middle of the page the order says: "First to execute the mobilisation of, A, units of the 1st command" and then below that "3rd to 1st, 23rd Light Infantry Brigade, on the next day, 8 June, 2001, and then B, units of the 2nd army command, below that 2nd/15th Infantry Brigade on the 8th of June, 2001, at 0100 hours," and then below that, "Howitzer division, 122-millimetre/15th Infantry Brigade on the 8th of June, 2001 at 0100 hours." Do you see what I've been reading, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of the order says that: "The units should be completed up to full military formation with people and material-technical means. In case there is a lack of people according to the staffing plan, non-deployed military conscripts should also be summoned." What, if anything, did you find significant in this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: The document clearly speaks about mobilisation. The document is also dated 7 June 2001, which means that there was a mobilisation process going on in the country in June 2001. The president authorised mobilisation of the, as far as I can see 3rd company of the 1st Battalion of the 23rd Light Infantry Brigade on the next day, 8 June 2001, at 1.00 in the morning. That is, this mobilisation was supposed to be completed within a very short period of time, within a few hours, which would serve as an indication to me that a very rapid build-up of forces was going on. The same point applies to the units of the 2nd army command, by the way, if I could make a comment. Apparently there is a slight problem with the translation here. It should be probably 2nd army corps not army command. The second point applies to units which again were supposed to be mobilised on the same day at the same hour, and these would be the 2nd Battalion of the 15th Infantry Brigade and Howitzer Battalion, not division. I would say Howitzer Battalion of the 122-millimetres of the 15th Infantry Brigade. So just to summarize, this document speaks about a few things. First of all, mobilisation process was going on where additional units were being mobilised and apparently the mobilisation process was not really proceeding very well, because point 2 of this document speaks about in case there is a lack of people, which would suggest to me that not all reservists were reporting on their calls for moblisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what significance, if any, is there to the fact that a Howitzer battalion was being mobilised? First of all, let's -- I should start earlier, can you please explain to the Judges what is a Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Howitzer is an artillery weapon with the range depending on the model of up to 20 kilometres perhaps, which is specifically used for destruction of hard targets, as well as for destruction of enemy manpower in the field. This is pretty serious weapon and 120-millimetre calibre would suggest that this is a pretty strong system.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The fact that a Howitzer battalion is being put into place what, if anything, would that suggest about the combat situation on the ground facing the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: My interpretation of this fact would be that the Macedonian security forces were facing pretty serious situation on the ground and they really required artillery support.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What significance, if any, do you see in the fact that such mobilisation had to be carried out so quickly, as you put it, in a matter of hours?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I would attribute it to the fact that there were certain developments of adverse nature on the ground, which would require mobilisation of these units. On the other hand, this could be also be explained by the fact that the Macedonian military and the General Staff were planning some kind of an operation which would require a certain build-up of forces in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be Exhibit P476.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 19 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 367.38. It is not specifically referred to in Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a -- an order issued by President Boris Trajkovski on the 8th of June, 2001, so one day after the preceding document. It is entitled mobilisation of a part of the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia and the order: "Part 1, to execute the mobilisation of the 1st and 2nd parts of the 25th Light Infantry Brigade, 2, that mobilisation should start on the following day at 1.00 in the morning; 3, the unit should be completed up to full military formation with human resources and material technical means; and, again, in case of a lack of human resources according to the staffing plan, non-deployed military conscripts should also be summoned." What, if anything, did you find in this document that was significant?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This document clearly speaks about mobilisation continuing. The document is dated 8 June 2001 which means that this date the mobilisation of the 25th Light Infantry Brigade was going on. Again, mobilisation was done in a very urgent manner which was probably dictated by the situation on the ground. It also speaks about mobilisation of the part of the units of the army of Republic of Macedonia which gives me reason to believe that this mobilisation was partial, in effect. And I would also infer from point 3 of the document that mobilisation was really facing difficulties as it says about involvement of non-deployed military conscripts in case there is a shortage of manpower.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour it is will be Exhibit P477.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you turn, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 20 of your document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 367.39. It's referred to in footnote 466 of Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report and my colleague Ms. Motoike has kindly reminded me to clarify that where I have provided references to specific footnotes for these documents, those references may not be 100 per cent, there may actually be other references located in the footnotes but we simply could not list all of them for each document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is another order issued by President Trajkovski. This is on the 9th of June, 2001. It says mobilisation of a part of the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. And the order says: "1, to execute the mobilisation of the Artillery Division," perhaps it should be battalion, you may correct us in a moment, "of multi-barrel rocket launchers 128-millimetres OGAN, flame, of the 1st Motorized Artillery Regiment, 1st command." "2, the mobilisation should start on 11 June 2001 at 0100 hours." And we see the same language in three and four that we saw in the prior two documents regarding the unit should be completed up to full military formations but if there are -- if there is a lack of human resources, non-deployed military conscripts should also be summoned. What, if anything, of significance did you find in this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: The general situation, Your Honour, would be the fact that mobilisation campaign was continuing, that new units were being mobilised, that more and more weapons would be mobilised as well. This is indeed an artillery battalion. I don't think this is an artillery division. This must be some kind of translation thing. And this particular battalion was equipped with multi-barrel rocket launchers of OGAN model, which is a Yugoslav model which was widely produced in former Yugoslavia. Its calibre is 128 millimetres. This is essentially an aerial type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you say area or aerial?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Area.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes. That is not a pinpoint weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does that mean then?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This means that, in fact, this weapon is a vehicle with several rocket tubes mounted on it, depends how many depending on the model. I believe in the case of this one it could be about 12. And this is the weapon which is used to mainly, according to classical doctrine again, to destroy the enemy manpower exposed in an open ground, open terrain over a big area. Well, in fact one [Indiscernible] of such a weapon would cover several hectares of ground with deadly fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be Exhibit P478.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we break, perhaps, I have one more question about this document, Mr. Bezruchenko. The fact that the Macedonian security forces felt compelled to bring this kind of weapon into operation against the NLA, what, if anything, does it suggest about the strength, the size of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Well, this weapon is pretty effective in fact and this is also good for moral effect. I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you say moral or morale?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Well, morale effect, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Morale.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Of course. Which means that it would effect the morale of the adversary forces. I think that the fact that this specific battalion was being mobilised would indicate that these kind of weapons was counted upon and was called for to carry on operations against NLA, which apparently showed a strength to a degree that required deployment of such weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Strength of whom?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Strength of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be a convenient time to take the second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. We resume in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, could you please turn to the document at tab 21 of your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter number 367.40. It's referenced in footnote 424 of Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is another decision issued by the president of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. It's dated the 11th of June, 2001. The title is to form the defence command of the city of Skopje. And then underneath the word decision in bold, point 1 says the: "The training command should establish the defence command of the city (DCC) of Skopje." Point 2 says: "To the composition of the DCC of Skopje should be subordinated the 12th Infantry Brigade, the 16th Infantry Brigade, the 1st Guard Brigade and the 8th Infantry Brigade." And then point 3, it says: "The chief of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia will issue orders for engaging the units for the defence of the city of Skopje." Mr. Bezruchenko, what, if anything, did you find significant in this decision of 11 June 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This document has to be analysed in the context of the developments and events at the front in June 2001. It should be recalled that on or about 10 June 2001, the NLA entered the village of Aracinovo which is essentially a suburb of Skopje. Thus, a significant threat, a pronounced, significant threat developed for the capital. This document apparently authorises the establishment of the defence command for the city of Skopje, which means that, first, the city was under threat; second, urgent measures were to be taken to counter this threat; and, third, sufficient troops had to be mobilised to ensure the perimeter defence of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see here point 2 of the decision refers to four brigades: The 12th Infantry, the 16th Infantry, the 1st Guard Brigade, and the 8th Infantry Brigade. Can you explain to us, just in general terms, how much men and materiel is that, men and women and materiel?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: In fact, that depends on formation. But my assessment would be that an infantry brigade composed of, say, three infantry battalions and artillery battalion, the brigade command and some supporting units would be perhaps between 2 and 3.000 men. This would be the formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that for a brigade that meets so-called NATO standards?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I understand at the time of conflict the army of Macedonia was in fact in the process of being adjusted to the NATO standards including the standards of the formations and units, and I'm not sure if this process was completely over, if it was absolutely complete by the time the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So, then, four infantry brigades would be somewhere between 8.000 and 12.000 persons. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: That would be a fair assessment, though I think in reality it would be closer to 8.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would -- Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I believe it is already an exhibit, 1D99.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What was causing me a distraction at that moment and I'll mention if you wish to explore it. Is the witness saying, then, that far more troops were deployed than were necessary? The earlier estimate of 2 to 3.000 men and then 8.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, my understanding of the transcript and the witness's response is that the estimate of 2 to 3.000 men referred to a single brigade and my question referring to 8 to 12 would be multiplying that by four because this decision refers to four brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That removes my confusion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 22 in your binder. Before we focus on tab 22, the previous document is referred to at footnote 424 of Mr. Bezruchenko's report. The document at tab 22, Your Honours, is 65 ter 367.41. It is referred to at footnote 425 of Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report. Mr. Bezruchenko, this document, it is another order issued by president Boris Trajkovski. It is dated, again, the 11th of June, 2001. The title says: Mobilisation of part of the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. And the order says, point 1: "To carry out the mobilisation of 12th Infantry Brigade, 16th Infantry Brigade, 1st Guard Brigade and 8th Infantry Brigade." I believe these are the same brigades referred to in the prior document. It says that: "The mobilisation of the mentioned units should be carried out on 12 June 2001, the next day at 0100 hours." The units -- this is point 3. "The units to be filled up to full combat formation with people and material technical means. If there is a lack of people according to the plan for filling up, the unassigned military conscripts should be called in." Point 4 says this: "The engagement of the mobilised units to be regulated by the personal command of the chief of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." Mr. Bezruchenko -- excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, my colleagues have just informed me that this document has been admitted it is 1D00-100.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what significance, if any, did you find in this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This is in fact the document, this is a -- in fact, a follow-up document in pursuit of an implementation of the decision by the president dated 11 June about formation of the Skopje defence command. Obviously, these brigades had to be mobilised to make for the defence of the city of Skopje. The next point I would infer from this document is that the mobilisation process was hasty and urgent, as is obvious from point 2 of the document it was supposed to be completed by 1.00 in the morning on the next day. The document then speaks about a potential of understrengths in the process of mobilisation. It mentions in point 3 that a lack of personnel, according to the plan, could be expected and in this case unassigned military conscripts should be called in. And finally this document, apparently, is pretty important because the responsibility, or rather, the personal command of the units assigned to the city defence command would be entrusted to the chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why is that significant?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Because -- because the Chief of Staff was, in fact, exercising the professional and direct command of the armed forces. He would be the person who would know exactly how the situation on the ground developed and he would be the person to take any appropriate measures, if required.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Can we turn to what is tab 23 in your binder, Mr. Bezruchenko, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document is 65 ter number 367.43. It is not specifically referenced in Mr. Bezruchenko's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is another order marked urgent, issued by the president of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. This one was issued on the 13th of June, 2001. It is entitled mobilisation of a part of the units of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. And it says, the order says point 1: "To execute the mobilisation of 2nd reconnaissance company of the 2nd" -- it says 2nd army command. I wonder whether it should say 2nd army corps. "City of Ohrid defence command and 2nd Howitzer Division," that should probably be battalion, "122-millimetre from battalion infantry brigade." Also, to mobilise the 7th Motor Brigade and a platoon. Below that a 120-millimetre Infantry Brigade, another light infantry brigade and a motorised division and below that a Howitzer division - that should probably be battalion - 152-millimetre. "Mobilisation should commence" this is point 2,"on the 14th of June, 2001 at 0100 hours." Point 3, again, they want full combat formation but in the case of lack of personnel, they should be called up from the non-deployed military conscripts. Point 4: "The chief of General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia shall regulate the engagement of the units with his orders, in accordance with the developments of the situation." Just briefly, Mr. Bezruchenko, roughly what part of Macedonia is the city of Ohrid?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: It's south of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it close to the Albanian border?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's close to Albanian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And close to the border with Greece, is that true?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you find significant in this order?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: There is a number of points about there order which are significant. The order authorises formation of the city defence of the city of Ohrid, which, to me would be an indication that a threat was developing in the area on the part of the NLA, and measures had to be taken to ensure the defence of this city. The second point about this document is that a number of units were continued to be mobilised and these included various units, artillery, military police, infantry. The mobilisation of these units was supposed to be carried out on the next day at 1.00 in the morning which is again an indication of the urgency of the mobilisation and seriousness of the situation. Another point about this document is that mobilisation indeed was facing some difficulties as apparently not all the reservists were reporting according to the table of mobilisation and equipment and formation of the units. And, finally, the document authorises the chief of the General Staff, in fact, to commit the units and deploy them, depending on the development of the situation, which, to my mind, would indicate that negative developments of the situation at the front were anticipated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will be Exhibit P479.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 24 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is 65 ter number 367.54. It's referred to in footnotes 330, 349 and 482 of Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report, and footnote 149 of part 5, the chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this document, the English version it's titled resolution. It's signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. It's dated the 5th of August, 2001. And the title says: Use of the army of the Republic of Macedonia for completion of operation. And then point 1 of the resolution says the following: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia with necessary structure and force, is to enter the town of Tetovo with the aim of preventing its fall into the hands of the terrorist groups of the self-styled NLA and protecting the lives, safety and property of the citizens of Tetovo." Point 2 says: "The army of the Republic of Macedonia is to position itself on the Tetovo-Jezince road with the aim of securing the traffic and preventing the terrorist groups from penetrating from Sharda [phoen] towards the villages in Polok. The protection of the road is to be performed continually until further notice." Mr. Bezruchenko, let's focus just first on point 1. What, if anything, do you find significant in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I think this document is pretty dramatic in a sense that for the first time mentions a possibility of the city of Tetovo falling into the hands of NLA. It actually requires, as is obvious from point 1, for the army of Macedonia to enter the city and protect it against the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the second point, please, and Ms. Alvarez, if you can help us by bringing up again what is Exhibit P467. If you can take a look at the map of Macedonia. This is page 2 of the court binders, Your Honours. And I'm wondering perhaps whether we could focus in on -- shall we say, the area of -- between Tetovo and Skopje and the border, the border with Kosovo. If we can focus in on that area a little bit, please. That's fine. That's fine. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, just so that the record is clear and perhaps with the assistance of the usher there is a pen there that's attached to that computer terminal, and I'd like to ask you, first of all, just to point with that pen on the screen there which road point 2 is talking about, the Tetovo-Jezince road.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: My understanding is that this is the road between Tetovo, which is here, up north, Tearce, Radnica and up to the border, right up to the border in fact, this is where Jezince is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can the record, please reflect that the witness has drawn a red line along a road going north-east from Tetovo towards the border with Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And before I forget may this image be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will be Exhibit P480.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what significance, if any, do you take from the instructions provided in point 2?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I believe it was pretty important to ensure the control of this road and prevent the NLA from using it. If the NLA established the full control of the road and the adjacent area, the NLA could actually enhance its capabilities as to supply across the border from Kosovo. The NLA could bring in anything it really wanted along this road, just by trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will be Exhibit P481.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is tab 25 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is Exhibit 2D00-040. It is referred to in Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report, footnotes 265, 266, and 273.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to explore this document with you a bit, please. It is dated the 9th of August, 2001. It's from the Republic of Macedonia Ministry of Defence security and intelligence sector. The Prosecution, Your Honours, received this document from the Macedonian Ministry of Defence. And it's a daily report for the period of 8 to 9 August, 2001. And it is multi-page document, but at the end it is signed by -- this is page 9 in the English version, head officer on duty, Mr. Georgi Karakutovski. In the first paragraph at the top of the page, we see that it is explained that in the period from 8 to 9 August in the duty operational centre of the Ministry of Defence the following operational data and information have been received. And then there are a series of paragraphs below that. Paragraph 1 says that: "On the 8th of August, 2001, on the road, Skopje to Tetovo, at 0930 hours at the location of Karpalak, Grupcin. Convoy of the arm of the Republic of Macedonia was attacked by the terrorists with Zoljas, mortar launchers and other automatic weapons. According to information obtained, 10 people were killed and 3 members of the security forces were seriously damaged. A Hermelin was destroyed and several military vehicles were damaged. The attack took place around 1300 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, if Ms. Alvarez can assist us, if we can see please, Exhibit 467, just the map at page 2 of the court binder. And, again, if we could focus, perhaps, or zoom in a bit on the area between Tetovo and the city of Skopje. That's it. That's fine. Perhaps if we could zoom a bit to the left just so that we can see the city of Tetovo. That's it. That is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Bezruchenko, could you take up that electronic pen again and on the computer screen, could you draw another red line on the road that's being discussed in point 1 between -- Tetovo to Grupcin?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This road actually connects Skopje and Tetovo and this is the road I mean. Grupcin is here as you can see, and goes on to Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, for the record that the witness has drawn a -- a red line along the road. Could you place the number 1, Mr. Bezruchenko, above the word Grupcin?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bezruchenko, what significance, if anything, did you take from the information that's provided in paragraph 1 of this report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: There is a number of issues which I would like to explain in connection with paragraph 1 of this report. Well, first of all, this attack resulted in ten personnel killed and three seriously wounded which was a pretty high level of casualties for this kind of attack. The other issue which I would like to explain that this probably happened because the commander of the unit did not really take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and security of his men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, we need to be careful here. Which unit are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: I'm referring to the unit of the ARM which was the target of this attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So when you say that the commander of the unit did not really take appropriate measures you're referring to the commander of the Macedonian army unit that suffered this attack?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: That's right, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: The other issue that I would like to explain is that this attack was apparently aimed to cut the communication between Skopje and Tetovo and deny the Macedonian army a possibility of bringing in reinforcements and supplies from east to west. That is, from Skopje to Tetovo. And perhaps the last point about this attack is that it took place, it occurred around 1.00 in broad daylight, which is difficult to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by that, Mr. Bezruchenko. What is the significance that this attack occurred at 1.00 in the afternoon in broad daylight, from a military perspective?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: From the military perspective, the commander of the unit, which was supposed to move along this road should have taken certain measures to ensure the security of his men, which would, at the bear minimum, include an advance party and patrolling along the routes, as well as probably observation points at some of the prominent features. Had this been undertaken, perhaps the attack would have been prevented, but I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you turn, please -- let's move to point 3. By the way, can you recall whether from your research whether this particular attack and the casualties had any additional consequences for the commanders of the army of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Yes. As I can recall, this attack was the immediate reason for the resignation of the chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we turn to point 3 from the first page of the operational information, we see that on the same day, 8 August 2001, at about 1200 hours, a group of members of the so-called NLA, 50 strong, armed with automatic rifles and Zoljas on the stretch from the agricultural school in Tetovo towards Motli [phoen] mosque began to set up control check-points. And then point 4, on, again, the same day, the 8th of August, according to operational information, 3 to 4 groups of uniformed and armed terrorists began an action in Tetovo with the aim to occupy noticeable facilities and buildings and some of them entered apartments, houses and shops. And those terrorists were looting and destroying households and furniture. What significance, if anything, do you take from points 3 and 4?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: My reading of these paragraphs was, in fact, the situation around Tetovo deteriorated to the point that NLA was operating in the city. The NLA started setting up check-points, they -- I mean, the NLA fighters began occupying facilities and buildings, perhaps placing their snipers, which would indicate to me that a significant threat for the city was developing. The city was on the verge of being taken over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to the third page of the English version of this document. This is page 2 of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see that I have neglected to tender the last image that is on the screen. If that could be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will be Exhibit P482.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, if we can turn to page 3 of the English version, page 2 of the Macedonian version, paragraph 8, which is at the bottom of page 3 in the English. Says, again, referring to the 8th of August, 2001, in relation to an attack against an army convoy which took place same day at 9.45 hours. It says: "Villages of Gurgurnica, Sedlarevo, Merovo, Raovik, Semeniste, Cajlane, Bukovik, Panicari, Laskarci, Novo Selo, Larce, and Kopacin -- Kopacin Dol were under the terrorist control. In that region, most possibly operates the 115th Brigade of the so-called NLA and one special unit of the military police." And then below that there's some reference to established check-points and the arms used by the members of the NLA. What significance do you take from this paragraph and the reference to the NLA's 115th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: This would indicate to me a pretty dramatic development as well. In fact, these villages are in the area of Zedan [phoen] feature, and along the road between Skopje and Tetovo, and the NLA taking over these villages would indicate to me that NLA was really consolidating their control of the road between Skopje and Tetovo. The 115th Brigade was indeed operating in this area, and as of the date of the report, apparently was holding the feature of Zedan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The feature of what?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO.
utterances.text: Zedan. This is a hill, prominent hill in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please. It is already an exhibit. I do not need to do that. And, perhaps, Your Honour, this would be a good time to stop for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The transcript should record the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: 2D00-040. Your Honour, before the witness leaves the room and we adjourn, may I raise one issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is simply this the normal rule and practice is that after a witness begins his or her testimony, he or she will not communicate with the members of the Office of the Prosecutor. Now Mr. Bezruchenko will have to come back and finish his testimony after Mr. Franz-Josef Hutsch finishes his testimony in two weeks. I simply wanted to note for the record, obviously, Mr. Bezruchenko works on the premises of the Office of the Prosecutor. There may be simply some unavoidable minimal contact in the hallways but there will certainly be no discussion with the witness about his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we must now adjourn until Monday week at 2.15 in the afternoon. And the witness, I'm afraid we must ask to return, I expect, late that week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of October, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
